item.title: Comparative Study on Land‐Use Trajectories Driven by Urbanization and Policy Implications in Wuhan and FCT ‐Abuja
item.description:
Adamu Bala, Xiaoqing Song, Houxing Gao, Xiang Li, Wei Huang
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70463
ABSTRACT Comparative evidence on urbanization‐driven land‐use trajectories across contrasting planning and governance contexts remains scarce, particularly among cities in the Global South, limiting understanding of urban growth and its policy implications. A comprehensive search indicates that no prior study has compared FCT‐Abuja with another city in terms of land‐use trajectories, urban expansion, and policy implications. This study therefore examines how land‐use trajectories and their policy implications differ between Wuhan, China, and FCT‐Abuja, Nigeria, using 25 years of global land‐cover data, reclassified into six classes, to analyze trajectories, growth rates, and landscape metrics. Significant and steady urban growth occurred in both areas, with Wuhan exhibiting higher absolute expansion and Abuja higher relative growth rates. Cropland remained dominant in Wuhan, while grass/shrubland declined significantly in Abuja. A total of 74 trajectory types were found in each area, with continuously stable trajectories accounting for 91.27% and 81.72% in Wuhan and Abuja, respectively. Edge expansion was the dominant growth pattern, with outlying expansion more prominent in Wuhan, while infilling increased in Abuja, with a late surge in Wuhan. Patch‐metric analyses showed that Wuhan exhibited higher values for NP, PD, LSI, LPI, and PLAND, reflecting differences in fragmentation, landscape complexity, and urbanization extent, whereas MPS showed contrasting temporal patterns, with Abuja recording larger mean patch sizes in the later period and lower patch density and shape complexity overall. The contrasting patterns reflect differences in governance, planning implementation, infrastructure development, land administration, and migration pressures, with stronger spatial control and increasing consolidation in Wuhan and more dynamic expansion in Abuja. The findings suggest strengthening land governance and control of informal expansion in FCT‐Abuja, while promoting compact growth and coordinated urban development in Wuhan.

item.title: A Graph Attention Network Method Coupled With Geographical Laws for Land Mass Valuation Under Limited Samples: A Case Study of Shenzhen
item.description:
Guang Li, Yuzhu Yang, Ying Liu, Haicong Yu, Chuan Lin, Qiulan Weng, Yuan Wang, Yilun Liu
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70462
ABSTRACT Constructing continuous urban land value surfaces is critical but consistently challenged by “limited samples.” Existing spatial interpolation and machine learning methodologies often fail due to over‐smoothing or insufficient theoretical integration. To address this, we propose Geo‐PHS‐GAT, a novel Graph Attention Network that systematically integrates the Laws of Geographical Proximity, Heterogeneity, and Similarity. The framework features three key innovations: a composite similarity metric for graph edge definition, a node feature vector fusing parcel attributes with neighborhood contexts, and a Transductive Learning strategy for information propagation from sparse labels. Applied to Shenzhen's residential land market, Geo‐PHS‐GAT outperformed nine baseline models, achieving the lowest RMSE in both Independent Out‐of‐Sample Validation (2943.07 RMB/m 2 ) and Leave‐One‐Out Cross‐Validation (7759.94 RMB/m 2 ). Mechanism ablation studies demonstrate that the synergistic coupling of all three geographical laws is essential for preventing value distortion, providing a robust tool for reliable land valuation in data‐scarce scenarios.

item.title: Differentiated Urban Transitions in China: Multidimensional and Multiscale Assessment of Population‐Land Interactions and Driving Mechanisms
item.description:
Feifei Lin, Xuesong Kong, Jinhai Li, Peng Cheng
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70458
ABSTRACT Dynamic interactions between urban population (UP) and urban land (UL) provide insights into differentiated urban transitions, but single‐dimensional or single‐scale assessments may conceal sustainability risks. This study develops a framework integrating dynamic coordination, utilization intensity, and distributional equilibrium across four geographical scales, treating administrative hierarchy as an institutional scale. It examines China's UP‐UL dynamics during 2006–2022 and diagnoses transition pathways and sustainability risks. Hierarchical linear models identify multiscale drivers and cross‐scale moderation. Results show that national UP‐UL dynamics tend toward coordinated growth, while provincial and urban analyses reveal divergent pathways, including imbalance and shrinkage. Administrative hierarchy is an important structural factor. Higher‐ranking cities tend toward intensive, population‐led development without necessarily achieving greater relative sustainability, whereas lower‐ranking cities face risks of shrinkage, sprawl, and inefficiency. Provincial institutional contexts directly influence population‐land dynamics and differentially moderate city‐level drivers. These findings support differentiated governance tailored to specific combinations of process, state, and pattern.

item.title: Intelligent Optimization of Public Space Allocation in Urban Renewal Using Ensemble Learning
item.description:
Bojuan Li
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70382
ABSTRACT Urban renewal programmes require spatially differentiated public space allocation across sites that vary profoundly in thermal environment, land economy, and social structure–yet prevailing practice relies on non‐spatial, single‐criterion standards. We present a spatially‐aware stacking ensemble framework integrating four geographically referenced data streams–administrative project records, resident satisfaction surveys, temporal behavioral panels, and Sentinel‐2/VIIRS remote‐sensing composites–across 3500 renewal parcels in China (2018–2025). A Ridge‐meta stacking ensemble achieves composite R 2 = 0.875 under stratified five‐fold cross‐validation; external validity is tested by withholding an entire climate zone from training: applied without retraining to each of the five withheld zones in turn, the framework retains R 2 = 0.837–0.858, so transfer into a thermal regime absent from the training data costs at most 0.038 R 2 , while withholding arbitrary spatial blocks of sites instead costs almost nothing. In practical terms, the ensemble leaves no detectable geographic pattern in its errors: residual spatial autocorrelation is statistically indistinguishable from zero, and the optimism of random relative to spatially blocked cross‐validation is only 0.004 R 2 , so accuracy does not rest on spatial dependence between neighboring sites. SHAP analysis identifies urban heat island intensity as the dominant spatial predictor and reveals a place‐specific equity asymmetry: thermal optimization penalties fall disproportionately on low‐land‐value communities, motivating thermally‐indexed progressive subsidy policies. SMOTE augmentation recovers severely underrepresented Park allocations (F 1 : 0.414 → 0.634), exposing a structural spatial bias against ecologically critical space types. The framework provides planners with an interpretable decision‐support toolkit whose limits of transfer are quantified rather than assumed. Its two equity findings map directly onto the Sustainable Development Goals: the thermal penalty borne by low‐land‐value communities identifies exactly where SDG 10 (reduced inequalities) requires compensatory cooling investment, while the recovered Park allocations identify where SDG 11 (inclusive, safe and green urban space) requires minimum green‐space quotas.

item.title: Diffusion Model‐Based Imputation Strategy for High‐Dimensional NetCDF Data
item.description:
Siyu Lu, Zhe Zhang, Nanzhou Hu, Jikun Liu, Yuhang Xie, Yuan Niu, Jinyu Zhou
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70461
ABSTRACT High‐dimensional environmental datasets stored in NetCDF format often suffer from sparsity, irregular sampling, and missing observations, which limit their utility for environmental modeling and geospatial analysis. To address these challenges, we propose a diffusion model‐based imputation strategy that uses generative learning to reconstruct multivariable spatial fields from incomplete temporal snapshots. The proposed method leverages multivariable dependencies among environmental variables, enabling the diffusion process to model complex multidimensional spatial patterns in NetCDF‐based geospatial raster fields. Experimental results on atmosphere datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently improves reconstruction accuracy compared to conventional interpolation and machine learning baselines, while preserving local spatial structures. This strategy provides a reproducible framework for imputing missing values in high‐dimensional NetCDF data, thereby potentially supporting more reliable environmental monitoring and resilience planning in GIS field.
